pages.text: "Wow! Glide!" Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, slid across the frozen puddle. Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, stopped before it and hugged the green bag.
"Try it, Gugu!" Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, glided by. "I want to. But falling hurts." Gugu shook the head, touched a toe to the ice, then pulled it back.
Gugu sat on the snow far from the ice, hugging the knees. Nono and Kiki glided past. "Only I cannot do it..." Gugu looked sad.
Grandpa Badger came from the shop with a snow shovel. "Want to hold my hand, Gugu? I will stay beside you." He held out a big, warm hand.
Gugu took it gently and stepped onto the ice. "You need not go all the way. Just a little glide." Gugu slid a short way. "I did not fall!"
"Now bend your knees a little. You will not wobble." Gugu did, and the body held steady. "Bend your knees and glide!" Gugu grinned.
Grandpa gently let go. With knees bent, Gugu glided to the puddle's far edge. "I went farthest! Bend your knees and glide!"
Two marks lay side by side on the ice: one short, one very long. Gugu touched the green bag strap. Nono and Kiki clapped.
Gugu bent the knees and stood first. "One short glide, two short glides, then bend your knees and glide far!" They slid along in a line.
Grandpa wrapped Gugu snugly in a big blanket. Even something scary can become fun if you try little by little. Gugu's cheeks glowed. "Bend your knees and glide!"
